chapter: Traditional style, ragtime orchestra and closing questions
title: Preservation Hall band visit to Bridgewater, Virginia
summary: Wood begins a story of a Preservation Hall band booked at Bridgewater College on a cold February day in the late 1960s.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, you know, speaking of that, Percy Humphrey, that reminds me of something else that I wanted to tell you about. That in, it would have been in the late 60s, I guess, in my little community of Harrisonburg, Virginia, which is nearby a place called Bridgewater, which has Bridgewater College. And I thought that Bridgewater College sponsored an appearance of a Preservation Hall jazz band in February one year. And these signs went up, and I was excited about that. And when the day came for their performance, I thought it was a February day, and it was really cold. It was about 10 degrees. And I thought I would go to the motel and just try to speak to the musicians and some of them and extend the word of will. Thank you very much. Thank you.
